q: 医生说我现在不能运动，所以这个周末我___都不去，只在家休息。
zh: 医生说我现在不能运动，所以这个周末我哪儿都不去，只在家休息。
py: yī shēng shuō wǒ xiàn zài bù néng yùn dòng suǒ yǐ zhè ge zhōu mò wǒ nǎ r dōu bù qù zhǐ zài jiā xiū xi
en: The doctor says I can't exercise now, so this weekend I'm not going anywhere and will just rest at home.
why: 'Not going anywhere' is 哪儿都不去, with 哪儿 in front of 都. 什么 or 谁 cannot be a destination.

q: 他每次开会___迟到。
py: tā měi cì kāi huì dōu chí dào
en: He is late for every meeting.
why: 每次 is followed by 都 before the verb. 也 would say he is late as well as someone else, and 才 or 再 do not fit with 每次.

s: 他八十岁都了，身体还很好。
s_py: tā bā shí suì dōu le shēn tǐ hái hěn hǎo
zh: 他都八十岁了，身体还很好。
py: tā dōu bā shí suì le shēn tǐ hái hěn hǎo
en: He's already eighty and still in good health.
why: 'Already' 都 comes before the age expression, with 了 at the end. 八十岁都了 reverses that.

s_py: wǒ xǐ huan hē chá yě
py: wǒ yě xǐ huan hē chá
en: I like drinking tea too.
why: 也 can never end a sentence. It goes after the subject and before the verb.

task: Say that you drink coffee too.
py: wǒ yě hē kā fēi
en: I drink coffee too.
why: 也 goes after the subject and before the verb. English puts 'too' at the end, but 也 can never end a sentence.

s_py: zhè jǐ tiān tā dōu zài yī yuàn
py: zhè jǐ tiān tā dōu zài yī yuàn
en: He has been at the hospital all these days.
why: 都 can total a time phrase to its left, so it is fine here even though 他 is one person.

q: 这些客户我___认识，只认识两三个。
zh: 这些客户我不都认识，只认识两三个。
py: zhè xiē kè hù wǒ bù dōu rèn shi zhǐ rèn shi liǎng sān gè
en: I don't know all of these clients; I only know two or three.
why: 不都 means 'not all', which fits knowing just two or three. 都不认识 would mean knowing none of them, which contradicts 只认识两三个.

s_py: wǒ měi tiān chī dōu zǎo fàn
py: wǒ měi tiān dōu chī zǎo fàn
en: I eat breakfast every day.
why: 都 follows the 每天 phrase and precedes the verb. It cannot be wedged between the verb and its object.

s_py: zhè xiē wén jiàn dōu wǒ kàn guo le
py: zhè xiē wén jiàn wǒ dōu kàn guo le
en: I've read all of these files.
why: 都 is an adverb and must stand directly before the verb, after the subject 我. It cannot sit between the fronted object and the subject.

q: 爸爸和妈妈___头疼。
py: bà ba hé mā ma dōu tóu téng
en: Both Dad and Mum have a headache.
why: Chinese has no separate word for 'both': two people joined by 和 are totalled by 都. 也 would need an earlier person who had a headache as well.

q: 我最近胃不舒服，不吃辣的，___不喝咖啡。
zh: 我最近胃不舒服，不吃辣的，也不喝咖啡。
py: wǒ zuì jìn wèi bù shū fu bù chī là de yě bù hē kā fēi
en: My stomach has been upset lately; I don't eat spicy food, and I don't drink coffee either.
why: 'Don't ... either' is 也不, with 也 before 不. 很 and 会 do not mean 'either', and 才不 would be an emphatic denial.

q: 同事们___很忙。
py: tóng shì men dōu hěn máng
en: My colleagues are all very busy.
why: 都 totals the plural subject 同事们 and sits right before 很忙. 也 would mean 'too', adding them to someone already mentioned, but the cue says 'all'.

zh: 办公室的人也都觉得很冷。
py: bàn gōng shì de rén yě dōu jué de hěn lěng
en: Everyone in the office feels cold too.
why: Both adverbs follow the subject and precede 觉得, in the order 也 then 都.

zh: 开会的时候他一句话也没说。
py: kāi huì de shí hou tā yī jù huà yě méi shuō
en: He didn't say a single word during the meeting.
why: 一句话 + 也 + 没 + verb means 'not even one word'. The negative 没 is required and comes after 也.

q: 每个同事___会用这个软件。
zh: 每个同事都会用这个软件。
py: měi gè tóng shì dōu huì yòng zhè ge ruǎn jiàn
en: Every colleague can use this software.
why: 每个 + noun calls for 都 before the verb phrase. 也 would add a second fact, and 就 and 才 give 'then' or 'only then'.

py: zhè xiē yóu jiàn wǒ dōu huí le
en: I've replied to all of these emails.
why: 都 can only total something to its left, so the emails move in front of 都. With 我 alone to its left, 都 would have nothing to total.

q: 每天早上我___先量体温，然后再吃药。
zh: 每天早上我都先量体温，然后再吃药。
py: měi tiān zǎo shang wǒ dōu xiān liáng tǐ wēn rán hòu zài chī yào
en: Every morning I take my temperature first and then take my medicine.
why: After 每天早上 the habit is marked with 都, placed before 先量体温. 也, 才 and 又 would change the meaning to 'also', 'only then' or 'again'.

q: 孩子___咳嗽了半个月了，你怎么现在才带他去医院？
zh: 孩子都咳嗽了半个月了，你怎么现在才带他去医院？
py: hái zi dōu ké sou le bàn gè yuè le nǐ zěn me xiàn zài cái dài tā qù yī yuàn
en: The child has been coughing for half a month already; why are you only taking him to the hospital now?
why: 都 ... 了 means 'already half a month', which explains the criticism that follows. 才 would make half a month sound short.

task: Make it negative: none of us went.
py: wǒ men dōu méi qù
en: None of us went.
why: 都 stays before the negative: 都没 means none of us. 没 replaces 了, and the two cannot appear together.

task: Say you are not hungry at all (一点儿 + 都).
py: wǒ yī diǎn r dōu bù è
en: I'm not hungry at all.
why: 'Not at all' is 一点儿, then 都 (or 也), then 不, then the adjective. The negative stays in the sentence.

py: yī shēng hé hù shi dōu xiǎng xiū xi
en: The doctors and nurses all want to rest.
why: 都 totals the joined subject and stands before the modal 想, not after it and not at the end.

q: 这几天我们办公室___很冷。
zh: 这几天我们办公室都很冷。
py: zhè jǐ tiān wǒ men bàn gōng shì dōu hěn lěng
en: Our office has been cold all these past few days.
why: 都 can total the time phrase 这几天 to its left (every one of these days). 也 would add this to some other place or time already mentioned, which the cue does not do.

py: zhè xiē yào wǒ dōu chī le
en: I've taken all of these medicines.
why: The medicines are what 'all' refers to, so they stand before 都. Putting them after the verb would leave 都 totalling only 我.

q: 这份报告我检查了三遍，一个错字___没发现。
zh: 这份报告我检查了三遍，一个错字也没发现。
py: zhè fèn bào gào wǒ jiǎn chá le sān biàn yī gè cuò zì yě méi fā xiàn
en: I checked this report three times and didn't find a single typo.
why: 一 + measure + noun + 也 + 没 gives 'not even one'. 就, 又 and 再 cannot take the 也/都 slot in this negative pattern.

q: 这些药我吃过，那些药我___都吃过。
zh: 这些药我吃过，那些药我也都吃过。
py: zhè xiē yào wǒ chī guo nà xiē yào wǒ yě dōu chī guo
en: I've taken these medicines, and I've taken all of those too.
why: The fronted object 那些药 lets 都 total it, and 也 ('too') must come before 都. 就, 才 and 只 would give 'right away' or 'only'.

py: zhè jǐ tiān dà jiā dōu zài jiā bān
en: Everyone has been working overtime these past few days.
why: 都 must follow what it totals and precede 在加班. The time phrase may come before or after 大家.

q: 我最近睡得不好，小王说他最近___睡得不好。
zh: 我最近睡得不好，小王说他最近也睡得不好。
py: wǒ zuì jìn shuì de bù hǎo xiǎo wáng shuō tā zuì jìn yě shuì de bù hǎo
en: I haven't been sleeping well lately, and Xiao Wang says he hasn't been sleeping well lately either.
why: 也 comes after the subject and its time word, right before the predicate 睡得不好. 都 needs a plural subject, and 就 or 才 do not mean 'either'.

q: 这个问题很简单，___都会做。
zh: 这个问题很简单，谁都会做。
py: zhè ge wèn tí hěn jiǎn dān shéi dōu huì zuò
en: This problem is very easy; anyone can do it.
why: 谁 + 都 means 'anyone', the person who can do it. 哪儿 and 怎么 do not name a person.

q: 我们___没有时间。
py: wǒ men dōu méi yǒu shí jiān
en: None of us has time.
why: 都 before 没 means none of us. 也 would mean 'we also have no time', and 不 cannot negate 有.

s: 每次开会，他都带着笔记本。
s_py: měi cì kāi huì tā dōu dài zhe bǐ jì běn
zh: 每次开会，他都带着笔记本。
py: měi cì kāi huì tā dōu dài zhe bǐ jì běn
en: At every meeting he brings his notebook.
why: 每次 is followed by 都 before the verb, so the sentence is correct.

zh: 这些病人不都需要住院。
py: zhè xiē bìng rén bù dōu xū yào zhù yuàn
en: Not all of these patients need to be hospitalised.
why: 不 before 都 means 'not all'. 都不 would mean none of them need it.

py: wǒ shén me dōu bù xiǎng chī
en: I don't want to eat anything.
why: What is eaten, 什么, moves in front of 都 and the negative follows. 我不想吃什么 would not give a firm 'nothing at all'.

q: 我的感冒___一个星期了，还没好。
zh: 我的感冒都一个星期了，还没好。
py: wǒ de gǎn mào dōu yī gè xīng qī le hái méi hǎo
en: I've had this cold for a whole week already and it still hasn't gone.
why: 都 + a stretch of time + 了 means 'already so long'. 才 would make a week sound short, and 也 would mean 'also'.

py: tā men yě dōu shì yī shēng
en: They are all doctors too.
why: The fixed order is 也 then 都, both after the plural subject and before 是.

s: 这些报告他们也都看过了。
s_py: zhè xiē bào gào tā men yě dōu kàn guo le
zh: 这些报告他们也都看过了。
py: zhè xiē bào gào tā men yě dōu kàn guo le
en: They have read all of these reports too.
why: The object is fronted so 都 can total it, and 也 stands before 都. The order 也都 is correct.

s: 他一口水也没喝就去开会了。
s_py: tā yī kǒu shuǐ yě méi hē jiù qù kāi huì le
zh: 他一口水也没喝就去开会了。
py: tā yī kǒu shuǐ yě méi hē jiù qù kāi huì le
en: He went to the meeting without drinking a single mouthful of water.
why: 一 + measure + noun + 也 + 没 + verb means 'not even one'. The negative 没 is present, so it is correct.

py: wǒ měi tiān dōu chī yào
en: I take medicine every day.
why: 都 follows the 每天 phrase and comes before the verb. It cannot go between the verb and its object.

s: 同事们不都来了，办公室里一个人也没有。
s_py: tóng shì men bù dōu lái le bàn gōng shì lǐ yī gè rén yě méi yǒu
zh: 同事们都没来，办公室里一个人也没有。
py: tóng shì men dōu méi lái bàn gōng shì lǐ yī gè rén yě méi yǒu
en: None of my colleagues came; there isn't a single person in the office.
why: 不都 means only some came, which clashes with an empty office. 'None' needs 都没.

zh: 最近我也常常觉得很累。
py: zuì jìn wǒ yě cháng cháng jué de hěn lèi
en: I've often been feeling very tired lately too.
why: 也 follows the subject (with its time word) and precedes the adverb 常常 and the verb. It cannot open or close the sentence.

q: 我什么___想吃。
py: wǒ shén me dōu xiǎng chī
en: I want to eat everything.
why: 什么 + 都 means 'everything' or 'anything' in a positive sentence, and 都 sits before 想. 也 is for negative sentences.

q: 这几个病人___没发烧，不用担心。
zh: 这几个病人都没发烧，不用担心。
py: zhè jǐ gè bìng rén dōu méi fā shāo bù yòng dān xīn
en: None of these patients has a fever, so don't worry.
why: 都 before 没 means none of them has a fever. 还没 would mean 'not yet', which is a different message.

s_py: wǒ men dōu yě qù kāi huì
py: wǒ men yě dōu qù kāi huì
en: We are all going to the meeting too.
why: When both adverbs appear 也 must come first: 也都. 都也 is not Chinese.

q: 我今天一点儿___不累。
py: wǒ jīn tiān yī diǎn r yě bù lèi
en: I'm not tired at all today.
why: 'Not at all' is 一点儿 + 也 + 不 + adjective. 还 would give 'not yet', and 就 and 才 cannot sit in this slot.

py: zhè xiē yào wǒ yě dōu chī guo
en: I've taken all of these medicines too.
why: The object is fronted so 都 can total it, and 也 stands before 都: 也都.

q: 头很疼，我今天___都不想去。
zh: 头很疼，我今天哪儿都不想去。
py: tóu hěn téng wǒ jīn tiān nǎ r dōu bù xiǎng qù
en: My head hurts so much that I don't want to go anywhere today.
why: 'Anywhere' with 去 is 哪儿, placed before 都 and the negative. 什么 or 谁 cannot be the place you go to.

q: 医生说我要多休息，我爸妈___都要多休息。
zh: 医生说我要多休息，我爸妈也都要多休息。
py: yī shēng shuō wǒ yào duō xiū xi wǒ bà mā yě dōu yào duō xiū xi
en: The doctor said I need more rest, and my mum and dad both need more rest too.
why: 'Too' plus 'both' means 也都, with 也 first. 就, 才 and 会 cannot take the 'too' slot in front of 都.

py: tā men dōu méi lái
en: None of them came.
why: 都 goes before 没 and means none of them. Putting 没 first (没都来) would turn it into 'not all of them came'.

q: 小王和小李___在新公司上班。
zh: 小王和小李都在新公司上班。
py: xiǎo wáng hé xiǎo lǐ dōu zài xīn gōng sī shàng bān
en: Xiao Wang and Xiao Li both work at the new company.
why: 都 totals the two people and stands before the 在 phrase. 还 means 'still', so it would not give 'both' at all.

py: xiǎo lǐ yě xiǎng huàn gōng zuò
en: Xiao Li wants to change jobs too.
why: 也 comes after the subject and before the modal verb 想. It is not placed after 想 or at the end.

s_py: tā yě zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò
py: tā yě zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò
en: He works at this company too.
why: 也 goes before the whole 在 phrase, right after the subject, so this order is correct.

py: wǒ men dōu xiǎng zài jiā shàng bān
en: We all want to work from home.
why: 都 totals 我们 and sits before the modal 想. It cannot follow the 在家 phrase or come after the verb, so 想在家都上班 and 我们想在家上班都 are wrong.

py: wǒ yě bù zhī dào
en: I don't know either.
why: 也 comes before 不, so 'not ... either' is 也不. 不也 is not possible in a plain statement.

py: wǒ men yě dōu qù
en: We are all going too.
why: When both adverbs appear, 也 comes before 都. 都也 is not possible.

q: 我每天___去公司上班。
py: wǒ měi tiān dōu qù gōng sī shàng bān
en: I go to work at the company every day.
why: A 每 phrase such as 每天 is followed by 都 before the verb. 也 would mean 'also', and 才 or 就 add timing meanings that the cue does not have.

s: 这几份报告都没有错，经理很满意。
s_py: zhè jǐ fèn bào gào dōu méi yǒu cuò jīng lǐ hěn mǎn yì

en: None of these reports has a mistake, and the manager is very satisfied.

q: 他___六十岁了，还每天去公司上班。

q: 他开了两个小时的会，一句话___没说。

py: tā kāi le liǎng gè xiǎo shí de huì yī jù huà yě méi shuō

py: tā měi cì dōu chí dào
en: He is late every time.
why: A 每 phrase is followed by 都 before the verb. The 每 phrase may stand before or after 他.

en: The doctor says I can't eat anything.

s_py: wǒ men chī dōu wǔ fàn
py: wǒ men dōu chī wǔ fàn
en: We all eat lunch.

q: ___十二点了，你怎么还不睡觉？

q: 办公室里的人___喝咖啡，所以没人去买。

q: 我头疼得厉害，一点儿东西___不想吃。

q: 小王是医生，我___是医生。

s_py: wǒ men bù dōu shì yī shēng
py: wǒ men bù dōu shì yī shēng
en: Not all of us are doctors.
why: 不都 is the correct way to say 'not all'. It does not mean none; 都不 would.

s_py: tā dōu shén me bù chī
py: tā shén me dōu bù chī
en: He doesn't eat anything.
why: The question word must come before 都: 什么都不吃. 都 cannot stand in front of the thing it totals.

s_py: wǒ de tuǐ yī diǎn r yě téng
py: wǒ de tuǐ yī diǎn r yě bù téng
en: My leg doesn't hurt at all.
why: 一点儿也 only works with a negative. 'Not at all' needs 不 after 也, so 一点儿也疼 is wrong.

src_py: tā men dōu xǐ huan jiā bān
task: Say that NOT ALL of them like working overtime.
py: tā men bù dōu xǐ huan jiā bān
en: Not all of them like working overtime.
why: 'Not all' puts 不 before 都. 都不喜欢 would say that none of them like it.

q: 这件事谁___知道。
py: zhè jiàn shì shéi dōu zhī dào
en: Everyone knows about this.
why: 谁 + 都 in a positive sentence means 'everyone'. 也 is for negatives, and 才 or 就 do not give 'everyone'.

q: 我不知道，他___不知道。
py: wǒ bù zhī dào tā yě bù zhī dào
en: I don't know, and he doesn't know either.
why: English 'either' is still 也 in Chinese, and it goes before 不. 都 needs a plural subject, and 他 is one person.

py: wǒ yī diǎn r yě bù lèi
en: I'm not tired at all.
why: The order is fixed: 一点儿, then 也, then 不, then the adjective. 不一点儿累 is impossible.

s_py: wǒ bù yě xiǎng qù
py: wǒ yě bù xiǎng qù
en: I don't want to go either.
why: 也 must come before 不: 'not ... either' is 也不. 不也 is not possible in a plain statement.

py: wǒ míng tiān yě qù gōng sī
en: I'm going to the office tomorrow too.
why: The time word may come before or after the subject, but 也 comes after both and before the verb.

py: bàn gōng shì lǐ shéi dōu bù chōu yān
en: Nobody in the office smokes.
why: 谁 + 都 + 不 gives 'nobody'. The question word stays before 都 and the negative 不 follows it.

s_py: yě wǒ jīn tiān qù yī yuàn
py: wǒ jīn tiān yě qù yī yuàn
en: I'm going to the hospital today too.
why: 也 cannot open a sentence or come before the subject. It follows the subject and any time word, then precedes the verb.

q: 我感冒了，___都不想吃。
zh: 我感冒了，什么都不想吃。
py: wǒ gǎn mào le shén me dōu bù xiǎng chī
en: I've caught a cold and don't want to eat anything.
why: What is eaten is 什么. The question word sits before 都 even though it is the object. 谁 and 哪儿 do not fit as things to eat.

q: 李医生在这家医院工作，他太太___在这家医院工作。
zh: 李医生在这家医院工作，他太太也在这家医院工作。
py: lǐ yī shēng zài zhè jiā yī yuàn gōng zuò tā tài tai yě zài zhè jiā yī yuàn gōng zuò
en: Doctor Li works at this hospital, and his wife works at this hospital too.
why: 也 goes after the subject 他太太 and before the whole 在 phrase. 都 would need two or more people to its left.

py: wǒ yě shì yī shēng
en: I am a doctor too.
why: 也 follows the subject and comes right before 是. It cannot go at the end the way English 'too' does.

zh: 他也想在这家医院工作。
py: tā yě xiǎng zài zhè jiā yī yuàn gōng zuò
en: He wants to work at this hospital too.
why: 也 sits right after the subject, before the modal 想 and the whole 在 phrase. It cannot follow 想 or the place phrase, and it cannot end the sentence.

q: 小王去开会，我们___都去。
zh: 小王去开会，我们也都去。
py: xiǎo wáng qù kāi huì wǒ men yě dōu qù
en: Xiao Wang is going to the meeting, and we are all going too.
why: When both adverbs appear, 也 comes before 都 (也都). 都也 is impossible, and 还 or 又 do not mean 'too' here.

q: 这次体检，公司的人___要抽血。
zh: 这次体检，公司的人都要抽血。
py: zhè cì tǐ jiǎn gōng sī de rén dōu yào chōu xuè
en: At this check-up, everyone at the company has to have blood taken.
why: 都 totals 公司的人 and comes before the modal 要. 也 would only add them to a group already named, and 只 or 才 give 'only', not 'everyone'.

q: 每次体检的时候，他___紧张得睡不着觉。
zh: 每次体检的时候，他都紧张得睡不着觉。
py: měi cì tǐ jiǎn de shí hou tā dōu jǐn zhāng de shuì bù zháo jiào
en: Every time he has a medical check-up, he is so nervous he can't sleep.
why: 每次 sets up a repeated pattern, so 都 goes before the verb phrase. 也 would mean 'also nervous', and 只 or 才 mean 'only'.

py: wǒ jīn tiān yě méi chī zǎo fàn
en: I didn't eat breakfast today either.
why: 也 comes before 没, after the subject and time word. 没也吃 is not possible.

q: 经理明天去上海，我___想去。
zh: 经理明天去上海，我也想去。
py: jīng lǐ míng tiān qù shàng hǎi wǒ yě xiǎng qù
en: The manager is going to Shanghai tomorrow, and I want to go too.
why: 也 follows the subject 我 and comes before the modal 想. 都 needs a plural subject, and 就想去 would mean 'just want to go', not 'too'.

py: tā dōu bā shí suì le
en: He is already eighty.
why: 都 before the age and 了 at the end give 'already so old'. Without 了 the sentence is unfinished.

py: yī shēng men dōu hěn lèi
en: The doctors are all very tired.
why: 都 totals 医生们 and stands before the adjective phrase. English 'all' after the noun tempts you to put 都 at the end, which is wrong.

q: 销售部的人是新来的，技术部的人___都是新同事。
zh: 销售部的人是新来的，技术部的人也都是新同事。
py: xiāo shòu bù de rén shì xīn lái de jì shù bù de rén yě dōu shì xīn tóng shì
en: The people in sales are new arrivals, and the people in the technical department are all new colleagues too.
why: The first group is new and the second is new as well, so 也 is needed, and it must precede 都: 也都. 才, 就 and 又 cannot fill this slot with the meaning 'too'.

py: měi gè bìng rén dōu yào chī yào
en: Every patient has to take medicine.
why: 都 follows the 每个 phrase and stands before the modal 要. Leaving it out or moving it after 要 is wrong.

q: 我昨天加班了，今天___要加班。
zh: 我昨天加班了，今天也要加班。
py: wǒ zuó tiān jiā bān le jīn tiān yě yào jiā bān
en: I worked overtime yesterday, and I have to work overtime today too.
why: 也 links today's overtime to yesterday's and stands before 要. 都 would need a plural to total, and 才 or 就 add the wrong meaning ('only then', 'right away').

q: 他头疼，我___头疼。
py: tā tóu téng wǒ yě tóu téng
en: He has a headache, and so do I.
why: 也 means 'too' and goes between the subject 我 and the verb. 还 would mean 'still', which does not link my headache to his.

s_py: wǒ zhè xiē bào gào dōu xiě wán le
py: wǒ zhè xiē bào gào dōu xiě wán le
en: I have finished writing all of these reports.
why: The object may sit between the subject and 都, as long as it stands before 都 so that 都 can total it.

zh: 今天的工作我都做完了。
py: jīn tiān de gōng zuò wǒ dōu zuò wán le
en: I have finished all of today's work.
why: 'All of the work' needs the object in front of 都. The object can sit before or after the subject 我, but always before 都.

q: 小李没去开会，小王___没去。
zh: 小李没去开会，小王也没去。
py: xiǎo lǐ méi qù kāi huì xiǎo wáng yě méi qù
en: Xiao Li didn't go to the meeting, and Xiao Wang didn't either.
why: 'Didn't either' is 也没, with 也 before 没. 都 needs a plural subject to total.

q: ___到下班时间了，经理怎么还在开会？
zh: 都到下班时间了，经理怎么还在开会？
py: dōu dào xià bān shí jiān le jīng lǐ zěn me hái zài kāi huì
en: It's already time to get off work; why is the manager still in a meeting?
why: 都 ... 了 means 'already', matching the surprise in 怎么还在开会. 才 and 只 would suggest it is still early.
